Below are the four new manifests — two per directory, added independently since `dev/` and `prod/` share nothing.

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  namespace: myapp-dev
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    env: dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: false
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  namespace: myapp-dev
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    env: dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  description: Read/write access to the myapp-logs-dev bucket only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  namespace: myapp-prod
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    env: prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: false
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  namespace: myapp-prod
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    env: prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  description: Read/write access to the myapp-logs-prod bucket only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

Attaching the grant to the existing principals

Each new `Policy` is a standalone customer-managed policy; it grants nothing until it is attached. In ACK IAM, attachment is expressed on the principal, so add the new policy's ARN to the `policies` list of the existing `User` (dev) and `Role` (prod) in each directory's `iam.yaml`. The existing assets-bucket policy entry stays as-is — this is an addition, not a replacement, so the assets bucket's access is unchanged.

In `dev/iam.yaml`, on the `User` resource:

```yaml
spec:
  name: myapp-dev
  policies:
    - arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/myapp-assets-access-dev   # existing, unchanged
    - arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/myapp-logs-access-dev     # new
```

In `prod/iam.yaml`, on the `Role` resource:

```yaml
spec:
  name: myapp-prod
  policies:
    - arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/myapp-assets-access-prod  # existing, unchanged
    - arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/myapp-logs-access-prod    # new
```

Substitute your real account ID (or use the same interpolation convention the existing `policies` entries already use in each file). If your `iam.yaml` instead expresses the grant with `inlinePolicies`, you can skip the separate `Policy` objects entirely and add an inline entry keyed `myapp-logs-access` with the same JSON document body under the `User`/`Role` — either shape satisfies the requirement, since the document's `Resource` is scoped to `arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-{env}/*` and never mentions the assets bucket.

Notes on the shape of this change

Both statements deliberately use only the `/*` object ARN, not the bucket ARN itself, because `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` are object-level actions; adding the bare bucket ARN would be inert and adding `s3:ListBucket` would widen access beyond what was asked. Prod uses no wildcard actions, satisfying the least-privilege criterion.

Because this arm has no base, overlay, or template layer, the dev and prod changes are genuinely duplicated: four files touched (two new per directory) plus one `iam.yaml` edit per directory. Editing `dev/logs-bucket.yaml` has zero effect on prod, and vice versa — environment isolation is structural here, but so is the drift risk, since keeping the two bucket definitions in sync is a manual discipline. Apply with the existing commands: `kubectl apply -f dev/` and `kubectl apply -f prod/`.
